title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Item 6 continues item 5 (compactification of the modular stacks M_{g,nu} and their 'structure at infinity'). Grothendieck takes a smooth connected variety X with a smooth (normal) compactification X^ whose boundary Y = X^ \ X can be taken to be a normal crossings divisor. The variety is apparently defined over a field of finite type or a number field, since an arithmetic Galois action appears later. He forms the formal completion 𝒳 of X^ along Y and the 'punctured formal tubular neighbourhood' U = 𝒳 \ Y, with U → X lying over 𝒳 → X^. This gives two exact rows of (étale, profinite) fundamental groups. Top row: 1 → π1^∞(X) → π1(X) → π1(X^) → 1, where π1^∞(X) is the kernel, i.e. the 'fundamental group at infinity' in the weak sense, normally generated by the inertia along the boundary components. Bottom row: 1 → π1^∞(U) → π1(U) → π1(𝒳) → 1, with π1(𝒳) ≅ π1(Y) (SGA1/SGA2-type invariance of π1 under formal completion). A vertical map α: π1^∞(U) → π1^∞(X) is induced. The point is that in dimension 1 the structure at infinity is just a family of inertia (cyclic) subgroups, one per cusp, each well defined up to conjugacy. In dimension >1 one needs the whole group π1^∞(U), which is the profinite fundamental group of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of Y, together with its Galois action. Grothendieck notes that π1^∞(X) is the closed (normal) subgroup generated by α(π1^∞(U)) but that α need not be injective. Programme: (i) make π1^∞(U) explicit, 'at least up to a point', in combinatorial terms (via some projective limit T, reading uncertain, and the stratification of the NCD Y); (ii) make explicit the Galois action on it; (iii) require, as part of an anabelian datum, that the outer homomorphism iα: π1^∞(U) → π1(X) be Galois-equivariant. He suggests checking this first for dim X = 2. The purpose is to formulate higher-dimensional anabelian or Teichmüller-tower statements (M_{g,nu} has dimension >1) in which Galois automorphisms must respect boundary structure. This is the higher-dimensional analogue of preserving the inertia classes at cusps, as in the definition of GT. Item 7 then begins on the complex Teichmüller space as the universal cover of the analytic orbifold M_{g,nu}^an.
errors: π1^∞(X) should be the closed NORMAL subgroup generated by α(π1^∞(U)); the subgroup generated by the image of a single conjugacy class of maps is not normal in general. The text says only 'sous-groupe (fermé) engendré'.

If Y is not connected (possible for normal X^ in general), U and 𝒳 split into components with distinct base points. The bottom row should then be read componentwise or groupoid-wise, and α is only defined up to conjugation on each piece.

π1(𝒳) ≅ π1(Y) and exactness of the bottom row require the usual hypotheses (properness, connectedness of Y). In positive or mixed characteristic one should restrict to tame fundamental groups. This is not stated, but char 0 seems intended.

ideas.what: Fundamental group of the punctured formal neighbourhood of a boundary NCD (U = 𝒳 \ Y) and its comparison to π1(X)
ideas.modern_name: étale/tame fundamental group of a punctured tubular (formal) neighbourhood; 'fundamental group at infinity'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre, LNM 208 (1971), for the tame π1 of the formal neighbourhood of an NCD; later étale-homotopy versions of tubular neighbourhoods (Friedlander, Hoyois et al.)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck–Murre, 'The tame fundamental group of a formal neighbourhood of a divisor with normal crossings on a scheme', LNM 208

ideas.what: Need, in dimension >1, of a richer 'structure à l'infini' than inertia classes: the whole π1^∞(U) with Galois action, described combinatorially from the stratification of Y
ideas.modern_name: boundary / tangential-base-point data for Galois actions on π1 of higher-dimensional varieties (e.g. maximal degeneration, boundary compatibility in Teichmüller towers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Nakamura and Nakamura (1990s), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), in the Teichmüller-tower setting
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme speaks of the structure at infinity of the modular multiplicities and the Teichmüller tower, but not of this diagram explicitly

ideas.what: Anabelian condition: the outer homomorphism iα: π1^∞(U) → π1(X) must commute with the arithmetic Galois action
ideas.modern_name: Galois-equivariance of boundary (inertia/degeneration) data; higher-dimensional analogue of preservation of inertia conjugacy classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in Drinfeld/Ihara GT and in Nakamura's and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps' work for moduli of curves

missed.claim: A general (not moduli-specific) programme to describe the étale fundamental group of the punctured formal neighbourhood of an arbitrary NCD boundary combinatorially together with its Galois action. The equivariance of π1^∞(U) → π1(X) would then be made part of the anabelian data, with a test case in dimension 2. In the literature this was carried out essentially only for M_{g,n} via maximal degenerations and tangential base points, not as a general higher-dimensional anabelian 'structure at infinity' with the possibly non-injective α as the key object.
missed.quote: Il faudrait expliciter, au moins à distance, en termes de "combinatoire" ... et de la structure de Y (qu'on peut supposer diviseur à croisements normaux) le groupe π1^∞(U) et l'action de Galois dessus, et exiger que l'hom. ext. iα : π1^∞(U) → π1(X) commute à l'action de Galois
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Bears on anabelian geometry of higher-dimensional varieties (e.g. hyperbolic polycurves) and on boundary-compatibility conditions defining GT-type groups. The non-injectivity of α (loss of boundary information in π1(X)) is a point rarely addressed explicitly.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear sketch linking Grothendieck–Murre's formal-neighbourhood π1 to a Galois-equivariant 'structure at infinity' as an anabelian datum in higher dimension. The ingredients are known and the Teichmüller-tower case was later developed by others. The general formulation and the emphasis on non-injectivity of α are only moderately notable.
transcription_corrections: 'défini de l.t.[?] sur le corps de nombres[?]' is very uncertain; the line may read 'défini de t.f.' / 'sur k alg. clos'. Trust the image; the base field is not clearly a number field.
'T = lim Hilb(h)[?]' is illegible; possibly a projective limit of π1's of neighbourhoods (lim← π1(U_h)) rather than Hilb.
In the bottom row the third term is π1(𝒳) (formal completion), with π1(𝒳) ≅ π1(Y) written below it.
Item 7 likely reads 'Sur l'espace de Teichmüller complexe M̃_{g,ν}^{an} = 𝓜_{g,ν}^{an} (rev. universel de la multiplicité [modulaire/analytique] M_{g,ν}^{an})', not 'l'organe des Teichmüller-tours'.
'sous-groupe {+fermé+}': the insertion over 'sous-groupe' may read 'fermé' or 'normal'.
